    needs: [scope]
    name: Firefox portable UI
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 20
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: frontend
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: frontend/package-lock.json
      - run: npm ci
      - name: Prepare Ubuntu archive source
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        shell: bash
        run: sudo --preserve-env=GITHUB_ACTIONS,RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT,RUNNER_OS "$(command -v node)" ../scripts/ci/ubuntu-apt-source.mjs
      - run: npx playwright install --with-deps firefox
      - run: node ../scripts/evals/portable-runner.mjs
        env:
          EVAL_BROWSER: firefox
          EVAL_TIER: ${{ (github.event_name == 'schedule' || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.extended)) && 'extended' || 'core' }}
          EVAL_SOURCE_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
      - name: Validate complete Firefox evidence
        run: node ../scripts/evals/browser-report.mjs eval-results/portable/firefox/${{ (github.event_name == 'schedule' || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.extended)) && 'extended' || 'core' }}/results.json
        env:
          EVAL_BROWSER: firefox
          EVAL_TIER: ${{ (github.event_name == 'schedule' || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.extended)) && 'extended' || 'core' }}
          EVAL_SOURCE_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
      - if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: portable-ui-linux-firefox-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: frontend/eval-results/portable/
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 14

  ui-gate:
    name: Playwright UI E2E
    needs: [linux, desktop, desktop-windows, coverage, packs, portable-evidence, portable, chromium-extended, firefox-extended, health, scope]

 for attempt in range(3):

  checks=pr['statusCheckRollup']

  pages=read(['api','--paginate','--slurp',f'repos/{repo}/commits/{a.sha}/check-runs?per_page=100&filter=all'])

 latest={}
 for r in sorted(runs,key=lambda x:(x['id'],x['run_attempt'])):latest[r['path']]=r
 runs=list(latest.values())
 failed=[{'id':r['id'],'name':r['name'],'conclusion':r['conclusion']} for r in runs if r['status']=='completed' and r['conclusion']!='success']
 completed=sum(str(c.get('status','')).lower()=='completed' or c.get('state') in ('SUCCESS','FAILURE','ERROR') for c in checks)
 names={r['name'] for r in runs};missing=sorted(expected-names)
 print(json.dumps({'at':time.strftime('%H:%M:%S'),'mode':a.mode,'sha':a.sha,'checks':f'{completed}/{len(checks)}','failed':failed,'pending':[{'id':r['id'],'name':r['name'],'status':r['status']} for r in runs if r['status']!='completed'],'missing':missing},ensure_ascii=False),flush=True)
 if failed:raise SystemExit(2)
 if not missing and runs and all(r['status']=='completed' and r['conclusion']=='success' for r in runs):break
 time.sleep(40)
else:raise SystemExit('Monitor deadline reached: acceptance still pending')

```bash
# a normal headless node
./mesh-talk-node --keystore ~/.mesh-talk/node.keystore --password "<pw>" --name "YourName"
# run as a store-and-forward relay
./mesh-talk-node --keystore ~/.mesh-talk/relay.keystore --password-file ~/.mesh-talk/relay.password --name "relay" --post-office
```

Parameters:

- `--keystore`: path to the encrypted identity keystore (created if absent) — **required**
- `--password` or `--password-file`: password that encrypts the keystore and
  relay log — **one is required**. A service should use a private regular file
  (mode `0600`) so its password is absent from process arguments and the
  launch-agent plist. Store that file in a directory accessible only to its
  owner. Back it up alongside the keystore; losing it makes the stored relay
  identity and ciphertext unreadable.
- `--name`: this node's display name on the LAN — **required**
- `--port`: TCP port for peer connections (default: OS-assigned)
- `--discovery-port`: UDP discovery port (default: 47474; local discovery shares a port, while routed probing can target an explicit remote port)
- `--post-office`: run in relay mode (stores-and-forwards recipient-encrypted
  opaque event wrappers for offline peers)

Desktop users can turn off use of discovered relays in **Settings → Connection & delivery →
Use post-office relays**. The per-device preference is on by default and takes
effect on the running node. Turning it off stops that device's relay uploads and
downloads, so offline delivery may wait until a peer is reachable directly.
Several relays may advertise on one LAN. Clients support a preferred directly
reachable LAN/Tailscale relay with eligible alternatives; an alternative must have
a surviving onward route for cross-site delivery. Independent mailbox-only relays
do not replicate automatically. Equal bridge relays can reconcile eligible opaque
mailboxes after explicit enrollment through a shared public trust manifest. See
[the federation deployment workflow](../docs/post-office-federation.md).

**Settings → Connection & delivery** also exposes independent relay sending/receiving,
public bridge discovery and physical-LAN-only discovery. Master-off overrides relay
data/directory participation without erasing saved preferences. See
[the settings contract](../docs/network-design-reference.md#4-settings-and-deployment-configuration).

The production relay rejects old
clear-header uploads. It cannot read the inner event or channel names, but
its authenticated connections and timing can reveal communication patterns.
Pending events stored only in the older clear-header format require the
original sender to retry through an opaque mailbox or deliver directly.
See [relay metadata privacy](../docs/post-office-metadata-privacy.md).

Discovery uses signed UDP **multicast** (group `224.0.0.167`, port 47474 by default);
peer connections are Noise-encrypted TCP on an OS-assigned (or `--port`) port. The host
firewall must permit UDP 47474 (multicast 224.0.0.167) and the chosen TCP port.

### Data directory ownership

The headless participant and post office acquire an exclusive OS lock on
`node.lock` in the keystore's parent directory before opening their identity or
message stores. Keep each independent node in its own data directory. Cooperating
updated CLI processes refuse a second owner, including while the first process
is still starting. The PID written to `node.lock` is diagnostic information;
file contents alone do not establish ownership. The CLI uses the shared core
`ProfileStorageLease` primitive. Dedicated post-office startup transfers the
acquired guard by value into its indexed storage owner without reacquiring the
same lock; participant startup retains its lexical guard.

The dedicated relay owns its maintenance, reconciliation, inbound sessions,
discovery and gateway proxy tasks. Unix SIGINT/SIGTERM stop admission, cancel
and join these tasks, and finish any admitted synchronous database slice before
releasing storage. A faulted database exits through this owner rather than being
advertised indefinitely; existing macOS/Windows service restart throttling remains
in effect. Windows forced Scheduled Task termination is a crash boundary and
needs native restart/WAL recovery verification, rather than Unix graceful-stop
claims. Aborted or reset accepts discard only that connection and yield before
continuing on the same listener. This includes Mio's bare macOS invalid-address
conversion error after a peer resets a queued connection. Interrupted or
would-block failures without progress use a persistent 20 ms to 1 s capped
backoff with fixed retry state.
Other errors retain their original cause and fail with accept-operation context.
Unrelated session completions do not reset an outstanding accept retry, and
shutdown can cancel it immediately. See [indexed relay resource bounds](../docs/post-office-federation.md#indexed-relay-runtime-and-resource-bounds).

The file remains after a normal stop or crash. The OS releases ownership when
the process's lock handle closes, including on termination. Restart the node
using its existing data directory to preserve its identity and queued events.
Do not delete or replace `node.lock` to bypass a busy-directory error: another
process may still hold its original file open. Use the service manager or OS
process inventory to locate and stop the actual owner first. Windows can block
reading PID diagnostics through another handle while the lock is held.
Permission or unsupported-locking errors need their own
resolution; they are not evidence that the directory is unused.

2. Prepare locked Rust and frontend dependencies from the repository root:

   ```bash
   make dev
   ```

3. Build the GUI version for your platform:
   ```bash
   make tauri-build
   ```

Desktop builds start without optional avatar, theme, or sticker packs and animated
Noto sticker files. Packs can be installed later from the marketplace or local ZIPs.
No edition flag is required. See
[`docs/CUSTOMIZATION_PACKS.md`](../docs/CUSTOMIZATION_PACKS.md).

For development with hot reload, use `make tauri-dev` after setup and keep its
terminal open. It starts the frontend server and desktop process; install the
package produced by `make tauri-build` when you want an application in your OS's
normal application location. Setup fetches Rust dependencies without compiling
the desktop before its frontend resources exist.

### Build Options

You can customize the build with the following options:

- Build for a specific platform:

  ```bash
  node frontend/node_modules/@tauri-apps/cli/tauri.js build --target x86_64-apple-darwin    # macOS
  node frontend/node_modules/@tauri-apps/cli/tauri.js build --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc # Windows
  node frontend/node_modules/@tauri-apps/cli/tauri.js build --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu # Linux
  ```

- Create a debug build:
  ```bash
  node frontend/node_modules/@tauri-apps/cli/tauri.js build --debug
  ```

### Installation Packages

Run these commands from the repository root. Installation packages are under the workspace
`target/release/bundle/` (or `target/<triple>/release/bundle/` for an explicit
target). The release workflow packages each target into a ZIP with
checksums and verification artifacts:

- macOS: `.app` bundle and `.dmg` disk image
- Windows: `.exe` (NSIS) and `.msi` installers
- Linux: `.deb`, `.rpm`, and `.AppImage`

## Platform-Specific Instructions

### macOS

#### Prerequisites

- Xcode Command Line Tools

#### Installing and verifying the macOS app

1. Download the `.dmg` file or use the `.app` bundle
2. Drag the Mesh-Talk application to your Applications folder
3. Launch from Applications or Spotlight search

Keep one installed application in `/Applications` and retain the same destination
during updates, for example `/Applications/Mesh-Talk.app`.
Keep build outputs and backup archives separate from that installation. After
replacing the app, verify its bundle identity, icon and the actual launcher entry;
opening an executable directly does not validate Launchpad or Dock shortcuts.
An obsolete launcher record can show a question mark even when the current app
exists. Qualify the stale record against its resolved file and bundle identity
before removing it, preserve other application records and layout, and verify
the remaining entry actually opens the installed app. Do not reset the whole
launcher database to repair one stale entry.

Local ad-hoc signing is separate from Developer ID distribution. Restricted
entitlements require the corresponding signing authorization; structural
signature verification alone does not establish that macOS will launch a
package. Verify the final installed bundle and its packaged copy on the target
machine. Keep the previous application recoverable until that launch succeeds.

#### Code Signing (for distribution)

For distribution outside the App Store, you may need to code sign the application:

```bash
# This requires an Apple Developer account
codesign --force --deep --sign "Developer ID Application: YOUR_NAME" /path/to/mesh-talk.app
```

### Windows

#### Prerequisites
[Tauri prerequisites](specifications/deployment_guide.md#prerequisites) for your
platform. On Windows, run the Make commands in Git Bash with Make and Python
available on `PATH`. Then:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk.git
cd mesh-talk
make dev
make tauri-dev
```

`make dev` prepares locked Rust and frontend dependencies and configures contributor
hooks. The Tauri CLI comes from those local dependencies; no global `cargo-tauri`
installation is needed. `make tauri-dev` runs the development app with hot reload
and keeps its terminal open; it does not install the app.

To install a source build, run `make tauri-build` instead of `make tauri-dev` and
open the package under `target/release/bundle/`. On macOS, open the generated DMG
and drag the app to Applications; use the EXE/MSI on Windows or DEB/RPM/AppImage on
Linux. The first build can take several minutes. The UI-free Rust core also runs as a
headless node, with a separate keystore for each instance:

```bash
cargo run -p mesh-talk-core --bin mesh-talk-node -- \
  --keystore ./alice.keystore --password-file ./alice.password --name Alice

Linux. The first build can take several minutes. The UI-free Rust core also runs as a
